It is intended solely for the use of current employees of Nexora Technologies Pvt. Ltd. Unauthorized reproduction, distribution, disclosure, or use of any portion of this handbook — in whole or in part — is strictly prohibited and may constitute a violation of applicable law and company policy. If you have received this document in error, please notify the Human Resources department immediately and return or destroy all copies.

Table of Contents Section 1 — Welcome to Nexora Technologies Section 2 — Employment Policies Section 3 — Code of Conduct Section 4 — Attendance and Working Hours Section 5 — Leave Policies Section 6 — Compensation and Benefits Section 7 — Information Security Policies Section 8 — Compliance Policies Section 9 — Performance Management Section 10 — Business Travel Policy Section 11 — Separation and Exit Procedures Section 12 — Frequently Asked Questions

1.0 Welcome to Nexora Technologies 1.1 Vision Statement Nexora Technologies Pvt. Ltd. envisions a future where artificial intelligence and enterprise software converge seamlessly to eliminate operational inefficiency, democratize data-driven decision-making, and empower organizations of every scale to compete on a level playing field. We aspire to be the most trusted and transformative technology partner for enterprises across Asia, the Middle East, and emerging markets — building systems that are not merely intelligent but genuinely purposeful. 1.2 Mission Statement Our mission is to design, develop, and deliver AI-native SaaS products and enterprise software solutions that solve real business problems with measurable impact. We achieve this by attracting exceptional talent, cultivating a culture of scientific rigor and ethical responsibility, and maintaining an unwavering commitment to customer success. Every line of code we write, every model we train, and every product we ship is guided by a single question: does this make our customers meaningfully better at what they do? 1.3 Core Values Integrity First We hold ourselves to the highest standards of honesty in all dealings — with customers, colleagues, regulators, and the public. We do not tolerate misrepresentation, shortcuts that compromise ethics, or conflicts of interest left undisclosed. Customer Obsession Customer outcomes are the ultimate measure of our success. We listen deeply, deliver reliably, and stand behind our products with the same conviction we bring to building them. Intellectual Courage We hire people who challenge assumptions, question consensus, and propose ideas that may initially seem radical. We believe the best innovations live at the edges of conventional thinking and that respectful disagreement accelerates progress. Ownership Mentality Every Nexora employee is expected to act as a steward of the company's mission, resources, and reputation — not merely as an executor of assigned tasks. When something is broken, we fix it; when something can be better, we speak up. Inclusive Excellence We believe the best teams are diverse in background, perspective, and life experience. Inclusion is not a compliance checkbox at Nexora — it is a strategic imperative and a reflection of who we aspire to be as an organization.

1.4 Company Culture Nexora Technologies operates at the intersection of rigorous engineering and bold product thinking. Our culture rewards intellectual curiosity, values transparency at all levels of the organization, and expects employees to grow continuously. We are a high-performance environment, but we measure performance holistically — impact over activity, quality over quantity, and long-term capability over short-term metrics. We hold regular All-Hands meetings, engineering open hours, and cross-functional working groups to ensure information flows freely and every employee has visibility into company direction. We celebrate failure when it produces learning, and we celebrate learning when it produces better outcomes. Psychological safety — the confidence that one can speak up, ask questions, and raise concerns without fear of retaliation — is foundational to how we work. 1.5 Purpose of This Handbook This handbook serves as the authoritative reference for Nexora Technologies' employment policies, workplace standards, and operational procedures. It is designed to provide every employee — regardless of role, level, or location — with a clear understanding of their rights, responsibilities, and the norms that govern our shared workplace. This handbook supersedes all prior versions and informal communications regarding the policies contained herein. Employees are expected to read this document in its entirety upon joining and to revisit relevant sections as their role or circumstances change. The Human Resources department is available to clarify any provision and welcomes questions through the HR portal or at hr@nexora.in.

2.0 Employment Policies 2.1 Employment Categories 2.1.1 Full-Time Employees Full-time employees are individuals engaged under a direct employment agreement with Nexora Technologies for a standard workweek of forty (40) hours. Full-time employees are entitled to the complete benefits package described in Section 6 of this handbook, including health insurance, provident fund contributions, performance bonuses, and learning budgets. Employment is at-will unless otherwise specified in a signed employment contract, subject to applicable Indian labour law. 2.1.2 Contract Employees Contract employees are engaged for a defined period or project scope under a fixed-term or service agreement. Unless expressly stated in their contract, contract employees are not entitled to the full benefits package available to full-time employees. Contract employees are, however, subject to all conduct, security, and compliance policies contained in this handbook for the duration of their engagement. Extensions or conversions to full-time status must be approved in writing by the relevant department head and the CHRO. 2.1.3 Interns Nexora Technologies offers structured internship programs across Engineering, Product, Design, Data Science, and Business functions. Interns are engaged for durations of two to six months and are compensated at a fixed monthly stipend. All interns are assigned a designated mentor and are expected to participate in the same code of conduct, security, and attendance standards as fulltime employees. Outstanding interns may be extended a pre-placement offer (PPO) at the discretion of the hiring manager and HR, subject to business requirements. 2.1.4 Probationary Employees All new full-time hires are subject to a probationary period of ninety (90) calendar days from their date of joining. During this period, performance is monitored closely through structured check-ins at the thirty- and sixty-day marks. Either party may terminate the employment relationship during the probationary period with a notice period of fifteen (15) calendar days. Successful completion of the probationary period is confirmed in writing by the employee's reporting manager and HR Business Partner. 2.2 Work Eligibility and Background Verification Nexora Technologies complies fully with all applicable Indian labour laws and employment regulations. All offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of a preemployment background verification process conducted by an authorized third-party agency. Background verification covers identity verification, educational qualification checks, prior employment history, criminal record checks, and reference checks spanning the previous seven (7) years. Any material discrepancy between information provided by a candidate and verification

outcomes may result in the withdrawal of the offer or termination of employment, regardless of the stage at which the discrepancy is discovered. 2.3 Onboarding Process The Nexora onboarding program is a structured thirty-day journey designed to equip new employees with the tools, context, relationships, and institutional knowledge necessary to succeed in their role. The program includes orientation sessions with HR and functional leads, product and technology walkthroughs, mandatory security and compliance training, IT equipment provisioning, access provisioning in accordance with the employee's role profile, and assignment to a designated onboarding buddy from within the team. 2.4 Employee Responsibilities Every employee of Nexora Technologies is expected to: perform their duties with professionalism and diligence; comply with all applicable laws and company policies; maintain the confidentiality of all proprietary and sensitive information; promptly report known or suspected policy violations to their manager or through the ethics reporting mechanism; keep their personal information in the HR system current and accurate; and actively participate in mandatory training programs as assigned. 2.5 Confidentiality Agreement All employees are required to execute a Non-Disclosure and Confidentiality Agreement (NDA) as a condition of employment. The NDA covers proprietary business information, product roadmaps, customer data, financial information, personnel records, and any other information designated as confidential by the company. Confidentiality obligations survive the termination of employment for a period of three (3) years, unless a longer term is specified in the individual agreement or required by applicable law. 2.6 Conflict of Interest Employees are required to disclose, in writing to the HR department and their direct manager, any personal, financial, or professional interest that could — or could reasonably appear to — conflict with their duties to Nexora Technologies. This includes, but is not limited to: employment or directorship at a competing company; financial interest in a supplier or vendor; personal relationships with parties in a business transaction involving Nexora; and outside consulting or advisory roles. Disclosed conflicts will be reviewed by the Legal and Compliance team, and the employee will be guided on appropriate steps to manage or eliminate the conflict.

3.0 Code of Conduct 3.1 Professional Behaviour Nexora Technologies expects all employees to conduct themselves with professionalism, respect, and integrity in every interaction — whether with colleagues, customers, vendors, regulators, or the public. Professional behaviour includes: meeting commitments reliably and communicating proactively when timelines shift; exercising sound judgment in the use of company resources; avoiding conduct that could embarrass, harm, or bring disrepute to the company; and maintaining composure and courtesy even in situations of disagreement or pressure. 3.2 Ethical Standards Nexora employees must not engage in bribery, corruption, fraud, or any form of financial impropriety in the conduct of company business. Gifts and entertainment offered by or to external parties must comply with the company's Gift Policy, which sets a threshold of INR 2,000 per instance and requires disclosure for any gift received above INR 500. Employees must not use their position or access to company information to derive personal financial gain. Any suspected financial misconduct must be reported immediately through the ethics hotline at ethics@nexora.in. 3.3 Communication Etiquette All internal and external communications must be clear, respectful, and professional in tone. Employees are expected to respond to emails and messages within one business day unless otherwise specified. Company communication channels — including email, Slack, Confluence, and Jira — must not be used for personal disputes, discriminatory or offensive content, or the dissemination of misinformation. Employees should use judgment in determining which communication channel is most appropriate for a given message and should avoid creating unnecessary notification noise for colleagues. 3.4 Dress Code Nexora Technologies maintains a business-casual dress standard across all office locations. Employees are expected to dress neatly and appropriately for their work environment. On designated client visit days or formal presentations, business formal attire is expected. Remote employees participating in video calls are expected to maintain a professional appearance from the waist up and ensure that their background is neutral, tidy, and free of distracting elements. Attire that is offensive, provocative, or emblazoned with content inconsistent with company values is not permitted on company premises or in company-branded video calls. 3.5 Respectful Workplace Expectations Nexora Technologies is committed to maintaining a work environment where all individuals are treated with dignity and respect. Employees must not engage in bullying, intimidation, verbal abuse, or any form of conduct that creates a hostile or demeaning environment for others. This

applies to all forms of workplace interaction, including in-person, written, digital, and remote formats. Managers bear particular responsibility for modelling respectful conduct and for promptly addressing any concerns raised within their teams. Repeated or egregious violations of workplace respect standards will be treated as serious disciplinary matters. 3.6 Social Media Guidelines Employees are free to maintain personal social media profiles and to express personal opinions in those forums, subject to the following constraints. Employees must not post, share, or comment on content that: discloses confidential Nexora information; disparages Nexora Technologies, its leadership, customers, or colleagues by name or implication; constitutes harassment or discrimination of any individual; misrepresents the company's products, financial position, or capabilities; or could be interpreted as an official Nexora statement without express authorization from the Communications team. 3.7 Company Representation and Use of Corporate Identity Employees authorized to represent Nexora Technologies in public forums — including conferences, media interviews, industry panels, and published articles — must receive prior clearance from the Communications team and their department head. The company's name, logo, brand assets, and registered trademarks may not be used in any personal project, freelance work, social media profile, or external communication without written permission from the Brand and Legal teams. All authorized use of the Nexora brand must comply with the Brand Guidelines published on the company intranet.

4.0 Attendance and Working Hours 4.1 Standard Office Hours The standard working hours for Nexora Technologies are 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM, Monday through Friday, inclusive of a one-hour lunch break. Total contracted hours are nine (9) hours per day and forty-five (45) hours per week, with eight (8) hours counted as productive work time per day. Core collaboration hours, during which all employees are expected to be available for meetings and real-time communication, are 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. 4.2 Flexible Work Policy Nexora Technologies offers a Flexible Work Arrangement (FWA) program that allows eligible employees to adjust their start and end times within a window of 8:00 AM to 10:00 AM for start and 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM for end, subject to manager approval and business needs. Flexibility is a privilege extended based on demonstrated reliability, role requirements, and team coordination. The FWA does not alter the total contracted hours or the obligation to be available during core collaboration hours. Employees on an approved FWA must document their arrangement with HR on an annual basis. 4.3 Remote and Hybrid Work Policy Nexora Technologies operates on a structured hybrid model for roles where remote work is operationally feasible. By default, employees in hybrid-eligible roles are expected to work from their designated office location a minimum of three (3) days per week, with the remaining two (2) days available for remote work. Specific team configurations may require higher or lower office attendance, as determined by department heads in consultation with HR. Remote work from outside an employee's primary city of employment requires advance notice to the manager and HR Business Partner. Extended remote work from another state or country — beyond two consecutive weeks — requires formal approval from the department head and the CHRO, as it may have implications for tax compliance, data security, and employment law. 4.4 Attendance Expectations and Late Arrival Policy Regular and punctual attendance is a core professional expectation at Nexora Technologies. Employees who anticipate arriving more than fifteen (15) minutes past their scheduled start time must notify their manager via the team's primary communication channel no later than their scheduled start time. Unnotified late arrivals are recorded in the attendance system and may be subject to corrective discussion. A pattern of unnotified late arrivals — defined as three or more occurrences within a calendar month — will be addressed through the performance management process. 4.5 Time Tracking All employees are required to maintain accurate attendance records through the company's designated time-tracking system (Keka HR). Contract employees are additionally required to

submit weekly timesheets for billing and compliance purposes. Falsification of time records, including clocking in on behalf of another employee or submitting timesheets that do not accurately reflect hours worked, constitutes gross misconduct and is subject to immediate disciplinary action, up to and including termination. 4.6 Break Policy Employees are entitled to a one-hour unpaid lunch break and two fifteen-minute short breaks during the standard workday. Break schedules should be coordinated within teams to ensure operational continuity. Managers may adjust break schedules for specific operational requirements with advance notice. Smoking or vaping is only permitted in designated outdoor areas and must not extend break duration beyond allotted time.

5.0 Leave Policies 5.1 Annual Leave (Privilege Leave) Full-time employees are entitled to eighteen (18) days of Annual Leave (also referred to as Privilege Leave or PL) per calendar year, accrued at the rate of 1.5 days per month from the date of joining. Annual Leave may be taken in minimum increments of one full day. Annual Leave requests must be submitted through the Keka HR portal with a minimum of five (5) business days' advance notice for leaves of up to three days, and fifteen (15) business days' advance notice for leaves of four or more consecutive days. 5.2 Sick Leave All employees are entitled to twelve (12) days of Sick Leave per calendar year, credited in full at the beginning of each calendar year. Sick Leave does not require advance notice and may be taken on the day of illness by notifying the manager and logging the leave in the HR system. For sick leaves exceeding three (3) consecutive days, a medical certificate from a registered practitioner must be submitted within forty-eight (48) hours of returning to work. Sick Leave cannot be encashed and does not carry forward to the following year. 5.3 Casual Leave Employees are entitled to six (6) days of Casual Leave per calendar year. Casual Leave is intended for unplanned personal matters and may be taken on short notice by notifying the manager before the start of the workday. Casual Leave may be taken in half-day increments. Casual Leave not utilized by December 31st of the calendar year shall lapse and is not encashable. 5.4 Maternity Leave Female employees who have been in continuous employment with Nexora Technologies for a minimum of eighty (80) days are entitled to twenty-six (26) weeks of paid Maternity Leave for the first two (2) childbirths, in accordance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 as amended. For the third and subsequent childbirths, twelve (12) weeks of paid leave are provided. In the event of miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy, six (6) weeks of paid leave are provided from the date of the event. Maternity Leave applications must be submitted to HR with supporting medical documentation at least eight (8) weeks before the expected date of delivery. 5.5 Paternity Leave Male employees and partners in same-sex relationships are entitled to ten (10) days of paid Paternity Leave to be taken within sixty (60) days of the birth or adoption of a child. Paternity Leave is available for a maximum of two (2) children. The leave must be applied for through the HR portal with at least fifteen (15) days of advance notice where possible. 5.6 Bereavement Leave

Employees are entitled to five (5) days of paid Bereavement Leave upon the death of an immediate family member, defined as a spouse, parent, sibling, child, or parent-in-law. Three (3) days of Bereavement Leave are available for extended family members, defined as grandparents, aunts, uncles, or first cousins. Bereavement Leave must be applied for in the HR system as soon as reasonably practicable and does not require advance notice. 5.7 Compensatory Off Policy Employees who are required to work on a declared public holiday or a weekend at the explicit direction of their manager are entitled to a Compensatory Off (Comp Off) day to be utilized within sixty (60) calendar days of the day worked. Comp Off entitlements must be applied for through the HR portal within five (5) business days of the qualifying work event. Unused Comp Off days that expire within the permitted window are forfeited and may not be encashed or carried forward. 5.8 Emergency Leave In exceptional circumstances — natural disasters, family emergencies, or sudden illness of a dependent — employees may apply for up to three (3) days of Emergency Leave per calendar year. Emergency Leave may be granted at the discretion of the employee's manager and HRBP, and the employee is required to provide supporting context within forty-eight (48) hours. Emergency Leave is deducted from the Annual Leave balance where available, or treated as Leave Without Pay (LWP) if the Annual Leave balance is exhausted. 5.9 Leave Approval Process All leave requests must be submitted through the Keka HR portal. The reporting manager is responsible for approving or declining leave requests within two (2) business days of submission. Leave may be declined when business requirements necessitate the employee's presence, provided the manager offers alternative dates within a reasonable period. The HR Business Partner serves as the escalation point in cases where leave requests are repeatedly or unreasonably denied. 5.10 Leave Carry Forward Rules Annual Leave may be carried forward to the subsequent calendar year up to a maximum of nine (9) days, subject to the employee's manager confirming that operational circumstances prevented the employee from taking the leave during the year. Carry-forward requests must be submitted to HR no later than December 15th of the applicable year. Sick Leave and Casual Leave do not carry forward under any circumstances.

6.0 Compensation and Benefits 6.1 Salary Structure Employee compensation at Nexora Technologies is structured as a Cost-to-Company (CTC) package comprising the following components: Basic Salary (40% of CTC), House Rent Allowance (HRA at 50% of Basic for metro locations and 40% for non-metro), Special Allowance, Employer's contribution to Provident Fund (12% of Basic), and a performance-linked variable component. Detailed compensation breakdowns are communicated to employees through their appointment letters and are available on the employee self-service portal. 6.2 Payroll Process Salaries are processed on a monthly cycle. The payroll cutoff date is the 25th of each month, and net salaries are credited to employees' registered bank accounts on or before the last working day of the month. Payslips are available for download through the Keka HR portal from the first working day of the following month. Any payroll discrepancies must be reported to the payroll team at payroll@nexora.in within ten (10) business days of the salary credit date. 6.3 Performance Bonus Eligible full-time employees participate in an annual performance bonus program, with bonus payouts typically processed in April following the close of the financial year. The bonus quantum is determined by a combination of individual performance rating (as assessed in the annual review cycle), business unit performance against targets, and company-level financial performance. Performance bonus is not a guaranteed element of compensation and is subject to the company meeting specified financial thresholds. 6.4 Insurance Benefits Nexora Technologies provides all full-time employees with a comprehensive group health insurance plan covering hospitalization, pre- and post-hospitalization expenses, day-care procedures, and critical illness. The default sum insured is INR 5,00,000 per annum. Employees may opt to enroll their spouse, dependent children, and dependent parents at a subsidized premium deducted from their salary. A Group Term Life Insurance plan with a cover of five times the employee's annual CTC is also provided at no cost to the employee. 6.5 Retirement Benefits All full-time employees are enrolled in the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) in accordance with the Employees' Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. Both the employee and the employer contribute 12% of Basic Salary to the EPF account. Employees with a minimum of five years of continuous service with Nexora Technologies are additionally eligible for gratuity benefits as per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. 6.6 Travel Reimbursement

Employees who incur travel expenses in the course of official company business — including client visits, inter-office travel, and company-mandated training — are entitled to reimbursement in accordance with the Business Travel Policy detailed in Section 10. All reimbursement claims must be submitted through the expense management system within fifteen (15) days of the trip's conclusion with supporting receipts. 6.7 Learning and Development Budget Every full-time employee is entitled to an annual Learning and Development (L&D) budget of INR 30,000 per financial year (INR 50,000 for Senior Manager and above). The L&D budget may be used for external courses, certifications, books, conference registrations, and professional memberships directly relevant to the employee's role or stated career development goals. L&D expenses are reimbursed upon submission of proof of completion and original receipts. Unused L&D budget does not carry forward to the following financial year. 6.8 Certification Sponsorship In addition to the L&D budget, Nexora Technologies sponsors specific technical and professional certifications identified as strategically important to the business. Sponsorship covers the full cost of certification examination fees and, where applicable, preparatory course fees. Employees who leave the company within twelve (12) months of receiving certification sponsorship are required to repay a pro-rated portion of the sponsorship cost. 6.9 Employee Wellness Programs Nexora Technologies invests in the holistic wellbeing of its employees through a suite of wellness programs including: a corporate tie-up with mental health platform Wysa for free counselling sessions; a sports and fitness reimbursement of INR 5,000 per year; quarterly wellness webinars on topics such as stress management, nutrition, and financial planning; and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) providing confidential support for personal, legal, and financial matters.

7.0 Information Security Policies 7.1 Acceptable Use Policy Company-owned devices, networks, systems, and accounts are provided for business purposes. Employees may make incidental personal use of these resources provided such use does not: interfere with work performance; consume significant system resources; involve illegal activity; expose the company to security or reputational risk; or violate any other provision of this handbook. All activity conducted on company systems is subject to monitoring in accordance with applicable law and the company's IT monitoring policy disclosed upon device provisioning. 7.2 Laptop and Device Usage Company-issued laptops and mobile devices must be protected with full-disk encryption, a screensaver lock activating after five (5) minutes of inactivity, and a strong login password. Employees must not install unauthorized software, disable security agents, or modify system configurations without approval from the IT Security team. Laptops must not be left unattended in public spaces. Any loss or theft of a company device must be reported to the IT Security team within two (2) hours of discovery, irrespective of the time of day. 7.3 VPN Usage Employees must connect to the company VPN whenever accessing internal systems, repositories, databases, or customer environments from outside a Nexora office network. VPN credentials are personal and must not be shared with any other individual. The company reserves the right to audit VPN access logs and to terminate VPN access for any employee who violates this policy. 7.4 Password Requirements All passwords protecting company systems must meet the following minimum requirements: a minimum length of fourteen (14) characters; inclusion of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and at least one special character; no reuse of the previous twelve (12) passwords; and mandatory rotation every ninety (90) days. Passwords must not be written down, stored in plaintext, or shared with colleagues or service providers. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all systems that support it, including email, VPN, and cloud production environments. 7.5 Access Control and Data Classification Access to company systems and data is granted on a least-privilege basis, meaning employees are provisioned only the access necessary to perform their current role. Access requests for elevated permissions must be submitted through the IT service desk and approved by the relevant system owner and Information Security team. Data at Nexora is classified into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Handling procedures for each tier are detailed in the Data Classification and Handling Policy available on the intranet. Employees must not store Confidential or Restricted data on personal devices or unapproved cloud storage services.

7.6 Intellectual Property All work product, inventions, code, designs, models, algorithms, and documentation created by an employee in the course of their employment — whether during working hours or outside of them, if related to the company's business — is the exclusive intellectual property of Nexora Technologies Pvt. Ltd. Employees assign all such intellectual property rights to the company as a condition of employment. Prior inventions that the employee wishes to exclude from this assignment must be disclosed and documented in writing at the time of joining. 7.7 Use of AI Tools Employees may use approved AI productivity tools for work tasks provided they do not input Confidential or Restricted company data, customer personally identifiable information (PII), or source code into any AI system not explicitly approved by the Information Security team. The current list of approved AI tools includes Nexora's internal AI assistant (NexBot), GitHub Copilot Business (for approved engineering roles), and Microsoft 365 Copilot where licensed. Use of public generative AI services such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude for tasks involving internal data is prohibited. Employees must review all AI-generated output critically and accept responsibility for content they submit under their name. 7.8 Email Security and Cybersecurity Responsibilities Employees must be vigilant about phishing, social engineering, and business email compromise attacks. Suspicious emails — including unexpected attachments, urgent requests for credential sharing, and unusual sender domains — must be reported to it-security@nexora.in using the Phishing Report button in the email client. Employees must not click links or download attachments from unverified senders. Clicking on a confirmed phishing link must be reported to IT Security immediately regardless of whether any credential was entered. 7.9 Security Incident Reporting Any actual or suspected security incident — including unauthorized access, data exfiltration, malware infection, device compromise, or accidental disclosure of sensitive data — must be reported to the Information Security team at security@nexora.in or through the IT Security hotline within two (2) hours of discovery. Employees must not attempt to investigate or remediate security incidents independently. Timely reporting is critical to limiting damage, and employees who report in good faith will not face adverse consequences, even if the incident resulted from their own error.

8.0 Compliance Policies 8.1 Anti-Harassment Policy Nexora Technologies maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward all forms of workplace harassment, including sexual harassment, verbal abuse, psychological intimidation, and any conduct that creates a hostile working environment. Sexual harassment, as defined under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act), includes unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, sharing of sexually explicit content, and any other unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature. An Internal Committee (IC) has been constituted in accordance with the POSH Act to investigate complaints and recommend redressal measures. Contact information for the IC is published on the company intranet and communicated during onboarding. 8.2 Anti-Discrimination Policy Nexora Technologies prohibits discrimination in any employment decision — including hiring, promotion, compensation, training, performance evaluation, and termination — on the basis of gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, caste, religion, national origin, age, disability, marital status, pregnancy, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Employees who experience or witness discriminatory conduct are encouraged to report it to HR or through the ethics portal. 8.3 Equal Opportunity Employment Nexora Technologies is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities in which we operate. All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and business requirements. We actively work to remove systemic barriers that may disadvantage underrepresented groups and conduct regular pay equity analyses to ensure compensation fairness across demographic groups. 8.4 Workplace Safety All Nexora offices comply with applicable occupational health and safety regulations. Employees are responsible for maintaining safe working conditions within their immediate environment, reporting hazards to the Facilities team, and following emergency procedures published at each office location. Ergonomic assessments are available upon request through HR for employees who experience discomfort from their workstation setup. Remote employees are responsible for ensuring that their home working environment meets basic safety and ergonomic standards. 8.5 Whistleblower Policy Nexora Technologies is committed to maintaining the highest standards of corporate governance and ethical conduct. Employees who become aware of potential violations of law, regulation, or company policy are encouraged to report their concerns through the following channels: their direct manager, the HR Business Partner, the Legal and Compliance team (legal@nexora.in), or

the anonymous ethics reporting portal at ethics.nexora.in. Reports may be made anonymously. Nexora Technologies strictly prohibits retaliation in any form against employees who report concerns in good faith, and any retaliation will itself be treated as a serious disciplinary matter. 8.6 Investigation Process and Disciplinary Actions All complaints received under the Anti-Harassment, Anti-Discrimination, or Whistleblower policies are subject to a formal investigation process. Investigations are conducted by a designated investigator or committee, are confidential to the extent practicable, and are completed within a target timeframe of thirty (30) working days from receipt of a formal complaint. Both the complainant and the respondent are entitled to present their account and supporting evidence. Investigation outcomes may result in disciplinary actions ranging from a written warning, performance improvement plan, suspension, demotion, or termination, depending on the severity and nature of the violation.

9.0 Performance Management 9.1 Goal Setting At the beginning of each financial year (April), every employee is expected to set measurable performance goals in alignment with their team and company-level Objectives and Key Results (OKRs). Goals are set collaboratively between the employee and their manager and documented in the performance management system. Goals should follow the SMART framework — Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound — and include both delivery metrics and behavioural competencies relevant to the employee's career level. 9.2 Quarterly and Annual Reviews Nexora Technologies conducts formal performance conversations on a quarterly basis, with a comprehensive annual review at the close of the financial year (March). Quarterly reviews focus on progress against goals, identification of blockers, and calibration of priorities. The annual review drives compensation decisions, promotion recommendations, and development plan updates. Employees receive a performance rating on a five-point scale: Exceptional, Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Partially Meets Expectations, and Does Not Meet Expectations. Ratings are calibrated across teams to ensure consistency. 9.3 Promotion Criteria and Career Growth Promotions at Nexora Technologies are based on demonstrated performance over a sustained period, readiness to operate at the next level, and availability of a role at that level within the team. Performance rating is a necessary but not sufficient condition for promotion: an employee must have received a rating of Exceeds Expectations or above for at least two consecutive annual review cycles to be considered for promotion. Promotion recommendations are made by the manager, reviewed by the department head, and approved by the CHRO. The career framework for each function, including role descriptions, competency expectations, and illustrative examples at each level, is published on the company intranet. 9.4 Learning Expectations and Training Programs Continuous learning is a non-negotiable expectation at Nexora Technologies. Every employee is expected to complete a minimum of forty (40) hours of learning per year, tracked through the Learning Management System (LMS). The L&D team curates a structured catalog of internal and external learning resources, including role-specific technical training, management development programs, product and domain knowledge courses, and cross-functional learning pathways. Managers are responsible for incorporating learning into team culture and for creating space for their team members to pursue development activities during working hours. 9.5 Employee Development Plans Employees who are working toward a role transition, managing a performance challenge, or preparing for expanded responsibility may work with their manager and HRBP to develop a formal

Employee Development Plan (EDP). The EDP specifies targeted competencies, recommended learning activities, milestones, and a review schedule. EDPs are living documents that are reviewed monthly and updated as circumstances evolve. The goal of the EDP is to accelerate growth, not to serve as a precursor to adverse action.

10.0 Business Travel Policy 10.1 Travel Approval Process All business travel must be approved by the employee's direct manager prior to booking. Travel costing in excess of INR 50,000 requires additional approval from the department head. Travel requests must be submitted through the Nexora Travel Portal at least five (5) business days in advance for domestic travel and fifteen (15) business days in advance for international travel, to allow for visa processing, accommodation booking, and cost optimization. 10.2 Expense Policy and Per Diem Employees are expected to book travel through the company's designated travel management platform (MakeMyTrip for Business) to qualify for automatic reimbursement. Economy class is mandatory for all domestic travel and for international flights of less than eight (8) hours. Business class may be approved for longer international flights for employees at the Director level and above. Per Diem rates for domestic travel are: INR 2,000 per day in Tier 1 cities (Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai) and INR 1,500 per day in all other locations. Actual accommodation expenses are reimbursed against original receipts within the category limits defined in the Expense Policy. 10.3 International Travel International travel must be pre-approved by the department head and the CFO for any engagement exceeding five (5) business days or a budget of INR 3,00,000. The company provides travel insurance for all international business travel through its group policy. Employees traveling internationally must register their travel with the HR department and carry a copy of the company's emergency contact information. Expense claims for international travel must include all original receipts and a brief trip report submitted within five (5) business days of return. 10.4 Visa Support and Client Meetings The Administration team provides support for visa applications required for business travel, including preparation of invitation letters, company registration documents, and travel history summaries. Visa processing fees are borne entirely by the company. Employees meeting with clients must adhere to the client's on-site security and visitor protocols and must not share any Nexora confidential information beyond what is authorized in the relevant customer agreement.

11.0 Separation and Exit Procedures 11.1 Resignation Process Employees who wish to resign from Nexora Technologies must submit a formal written resignation letter to their direct manager and the HR Business Partner. Resignations submitted verbally or through informal channels will not be processed until confirmed in writing. The resignation letter should specify the intended last working date, which must account for the contractually agreed notice period. 11.2 Notice Period The standard notice period at Nexora Technologies is ninety (90) calendar days for all full-time employees. For employees at the Vice President level and above, the notice period is one hundred and eighty (180) calendar days. Notice periods may be waived or shortened only with written consent from the department head and CHRO. Employees who do not serve the required notice period may be liable for payment in lieu of notice as specified in their employment contract. The company reserves the right to place an employee on garden leave during the notice period if deemed necessary for business continuity or data security reasons. 11.3 Knowledge Transfer and Asset Return During the notice period, the departing employee is expected to complete a comprehensive knowledge transfer to their designated successor or team members. This includes documentation of ongoing projects, handover of access credentials to system administrators, return of all company-owned equipment in good working condition, and clearing of pending expense claims. A departure checklist will be provided by the HRBP within two (2) business days of receiving the resignation. 11.4 Exit Interview and Final Settlement The HR Business Partner will conduct a confidential exit interview with all departing employees. The exit interview is voluntary but strongly encouraged, as it provides valuable insights for improving the employee experience. Final settlement — including outstanding salary, earned but unused leave encashment (for Annual Leave only, up to the maximum encashable limit), any bonus pro-rated to the last working date, and reimbursement of pending expenses — is processed within forty-five (45) days of the last working date. 11.5 Confidentiality Obligations After Exit All confidentiality, non-disclosure, and intellectual property assignment obligations undertaken by the employee during their tenure continue in full force and effect after the termination of employment for the periods specified in the respective agreements. Former employees must not retain copies of any company documents, data, or code beyond what is reasonably required for their own records, and must not solicit Nexora employees, customers, or partners in a manner
inconsistent with their post-employment obligations for a period of twelve (12) months following their last working date.

12.0 Frequently Asked Questions The following questions represent the most commonly raised employee queries. Comprehensive answers are provided to enable self-service resolution. For questions not addressed here, employees should contact the HR helpdesk at hr@nexora.in or raise a ticket through the Keka HR portal. 12.1 Leave and Attendance Q1: How many sick leaves can I take per year? Full-time employees are entitled to twelve (12) Sick Leave days per calendar year. Sick Leave is credited in full at the start of each year and does not carry forward or accrue. For leaves exceeding three consecutive days, a medical certificate from a registered physician is required. Q2: Can I take half-day Sick Leave? Sick Leave is granted in full-day increments only. If you need to attend a medical appointment during the workday, you may apply for half-day Casual Leave for that purpose. Q3: What happens to unused Annual Leave at year end? Up to nine (9) days of unused Annual Leave may be carried forward to the following calendar year, subject to manager confirmation that operational constraints prevented the leave from being taken. All remaining unused Annual Leave lapses on December 31st. Carry-forward requests must be submitted by December 15th. Q4: Can I encash my Annual Leave? Annual Leave encashment is only available upon separation from the company. During employment, Annual Leave cannot be encashed and must be taken as time off. Upon separation, earned but unused Annual Leave (up to the encashable maximum defined in your employment contract) will be included in your full and final settlement. Q5: How do I apply for Compensatory Off? Log in to the Keka HR portal, navigate to Leave Management, and select 'Apply Comp Off.' Select the qualifying work date, attach any supporting communication from your manager, and submit. Your manager must approve the application within two business days. Comp Off must be utilized within sixty days of the qualifying work event. Q6: Can I work from another city while on a remote work day? Yes, you may work from another city on your designated remote work days without formal approval for stays of up to two weeks. For extended stays beyond two consecutive weeks, you must notify HR and your manager and obtain formal written approval, as this may have tax and statutory compliance implications. Q7: Who approves Maternity Leave? Maternity Leave is a statutory entitlement and cannot be denied. The approval is processed jointly by your reporting manager and HRBP. Submit your application through Keka HR with a medical certificate from your gynaecologist confirming the expected date of delivery. It is advisable to initiate the application at least eight weeks before your expected leave commencement date.

Q8: Can Paternity Leave be taken in parts? Yes. The ten (10) days of Paternity Leave may be split across up to three separate instances within the eligible sixty-day window following the birth or adoption of the child. Each instance must be applied for separately through the Keka HR portal. 12.2 Remote Work and Flexibility Q9: How many remote work days am I entitled to per week? Employees in hybrid-eligible roles are entitled to two (2) remote work days per week by default. Your specific team's arrangement may differ; check with your manager and review your team's documented working model in Confluence. Q10: Can I work permanently from home? Full remote arrangements are available only for roles formally designated as Remote in the job architecture. For hybrid-eligible roles, a fully remote arrangement requires approval from the department head and CHRO and is not typically granted unless supported by a compelling business or personal circumstance. All remote exceptions are reviewed annually. Q11: I live in Bangalore but want to work from Hyderabad for a month. Is that allowed? Extended remote work from another city for more than two consecutive weeks requires advance notice to your manager and written approval from your HRBP. There are no standard objections to inter-city work within India, but your manager must confirm that your absence from Bangalore does not adversely impact team operations and client commitments. Q12: Can I adjust my start time under the Flexible Work Arrangement? Eligible employees may adjust their start time within the window of 8:00 AM to 10:00 AM, with a corresponding adjustment to their end time. FWA eligibility is based on your role type and manager approval. Apply for FWA through the HR portal, and your arrangement will be confirmed in writing after approval. Note that core collaboration hours of 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM remain nonnegotiable regardless of your FWA schedule. 12.3 Compensation and Benefits Q13: When is the annual bonus paid? The performance bonus for the concluded financial year (April–March) is typically paid in the April payroll following the close of the year. Bonus amounts are communicated to employees in March after the annual review calibration is complete. Q14: Am I eligible for the bonus if I join mid-year? Employees who join between April 1st and September 30th are eligible for a pro-rated bonus in their first year. Employees who join after October 1st are not eligible for a bonus payout for that partial financial year but become fully eligible from the following year. Q15: How do I enroll my parents in the health insurance plan? Parent enrollment under the company's group health insurance plan is available during the annual open enrollment window in April or within thirty days of your date of joining. Log in to the

insurance portal (accessible through the HR intranet page) and add your dependent parents. The premium for parental coverage is deducted from your monthly salary. Q16: What is the sum insured under the group health insurance? The default sum insured for employees is INR 5,00,000 per annum per family unit (employee, spouse, and dependent children). You may purchase a top-up cover at subsidized group rates through the insurance portal to enhance this coverage. Q17: How do I claim my Learning and Development budget? Submit a pre-approval request through the Keka HR portal under 'L&D Claims' before registering for a course or certification. After completing the course, upload the certificate of completion and original payment receipt. Reimbursement is processed in the next available payroll cycle after approval by your manager. Q18: Can I use my L&D budget for books? Yes. Books directly relevant to your professional development or role competencies are eligible for reimbursement under the L&D budget. Retain the original receipt and submit the claim through Keka HR. Fiction and general-interest titles that are not professionally relevant are not reimbursable. 12.4 IT, Security, and AI Tools Q19: Can I use ChatGPT or other AI tools for my work? Personal generative AI services — including ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, and similar tools — must not be used for tasks involving Nexora confidential data, customer PII, internal source code, financial data, or any other Restricted or Confidential information. For general, non-sensitive tasks — such as drafting public-facing communications, brainstorming, or learning about a technology concept — use of these tools is permitted at your own judgment, provided you critically review and take responsibility for all output. Approved AI tools for internal data tasks include NexBot and GitHub Copilot Business (for licensed engineering roles). Q20: What happens if I lose my company laptop? You must report the loss to the IT Security team (security@nexora.in) and your manager immediately — within two (2) hours of discovery, regardless of the time. The IT Security team will remotely wipe the device, revoke all active sessions, and initiate an incident investigation. A police complaint (FIR) must be filed within twenty-four hours and a copy submitted to IT Security. The cost of replacement may be partially or fully borne by the employee depending on the circumstances, as determined by the Security incident review. Q21: What should I do if I accidentally click on a phishing link? Do not enter any credentials if the page has loaded. Immediately disconnect the laptop from all networks (WiFi and VPN), and call the IT Security hotline. Do not attempt to scan or fix the device yourself. IT Security will guide you through the containment and remediation steps. Reporting promptly and in good faith will not result in disciplinary action. Q22: Can I install personal software on my company laptop?

Installation of any software not on the approved software catalog requires a request through the IT service desk. Unauthorized software installation — including consumer applications, games, cracked or unlicensed software — is a policy violation. If you need a specific tool for a legitimate work purpose that is not in the catalog, submit an IT service request and the team will evaluate it. Q23: How long should my password be, and how often must I change it? Passwords must be a minimum of fourteen (14) characters and must include a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters. Passwords must be changed every ninety (90) days. You must not reuse any of your previous twelve passwords. We strongly recommend using a company-approved password manager such as 1Password (provisioned through IT) to generate and store complex passwords securely. Q24: Is multi-factor authentication mandatory? Yes. MFA is mandatory for all systems that support it, including corporate email (Google Workspace), VPN, GitHub, AWS/GCP/Azure console access, and all production environment tools. The preferred MFA method is TOTP through an authenticator app (such as Google Authenticator or Authy). SMS-based OTP is available as a fallback but is not recommended due to SIM-swap vulnerabilities. Q25: Can I store company data on Google Drive or Dropbox? Company data classified as Internal, Confidential, or Restricted must not be stored on personal cloud storage services including personal Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive personal, or iCloud. Approved storage solutions for company data include the corporate Google Workspace (company-issued account), the Nexora SharePoint, and project-specific S3/GCS buckets provisioned by the IT team. If you are unsure whether a storage location is approved, contact itsecurity@nexora.in before transferring data. 12.5 Conduct and Compliance Q26: How do I report workplace harassment? You may report workplace harassment — including sexual harassment — through any of the following channels: directly to your HR Business Partner; through the internal complaints mechanism to the Internal Committee (IC) constituted under the POSH Act; via the anonymous ethics reporting portal at ethics.nexora.in; or by emailing ic@nexora.in. The IC contact list is also posted in every Nexora office. You may also seek informal guidance from any IC member before deciding whether to file a formal complaint. Q27: What if I witness harassment but am not the victim? Third-party witnesses to harassment are encouraged to report the incident to HR or the IC. You are protected from retaliation for reporting in good faith, regardless of whether you are the complainant. In situations where immediate harm is occurring, please intervene safely or contact the office security desk. Q28: Can I date a colleague? Nexora Technologies does not prohibit consensual romantic relationships between colleagues, provided both parties are at the same or comparable hierarchical level and there is no direct reporting relationship between them. Where a direct reporting relationship exists, one party must

immediately notify HR, which will facilitate a structural realignment to eliminate the reporting relationship. Non-disclosure of a relationship that creates a conflict of interest is treated as a policy violation. Q29: What is the disciplinary process for a policy violation? Minor first-time violations typically result in a documented verbal or written warning issued by the manager in consultation with HR. Repeated violations or more serious infractions may result in a formal Performance Improvement Plan, final written warning, suspension without pay, demotion, or termination, depending on the nature and severity of the conduct. Gross misconduct — including fraud, violence, harassment, and serious security breaches — may result in immediate termination without prior warning at the company's discretion. Q30: Can I speak to media about Nexora? No employee is authorized to speak to media, analysts, or journalists on behalf of Nexora Technologies without prior written approval from the Communications team and their department head. All media inquiries should be redirected to pr@nexora.in. Unauthorized statements to the media, even those made personally with a disclaimer, may be treated as a policy violation if they reference the company's business, products, or people. 12.6 Exit and Separation Q31: What is the notice period at Nexora? The standard notice period for full-time employees is ninety (90) calendar days. For Vice Presidents and above, the notice period is one hundred and eighty (180) calendar days. Your specific notice period is stated in your appointment letter and may differ from the standard if a custom arrangement was negotiated at the time of joining. Q32: Can I buy out my notice period? Notice period buyout — where the employee pays the company an amount equivalent to their salary for the remaining notice period — is not a standard option at Nexora Technologies. Shortened notice may be granted with written approval from the department head and CHRO on a case-by-case basis, taking into account operational continuity requirements. Q33: What documents will I receive after I leave? Upon completing your exit formalities, you will receive: an Experience and Service Letter confirming your tenure, role, and dates of employment; Form 16 for the relevant financial year(s); EPF withdrawal or transfer forms; and a relieving letter confirming your last working date and that all obligations have been fulfilled. These documents are typically issued within thirty (30) days of your last working date. Q34: When will my final settlement be processed? Full and final settlement — covering outstanding salary, earned leave encashment, any pro-rated bonus, and reimbursement of pending expenses — is processed within forty-five (45) days of your last working date. Settlement is contingent upon return of all company assets, clearance from IT Security, and no outstanding disciplinary or financial liabilities. Q35: Can I return to Nexora after resigning?

Former employees in good standing are eligible to be considered for rehire (commonly called 'boomerang hires') after a minimum of twelve (12) months since their separation. Previous tenure, performance history, and the circumstances of separation are taken into account. Rehire requires the same hiring process as any new candidate and does not guarantee reinstatement of previous compensation level, grade, or tenure. 12.7 Payroll and Finance Q36: What should I do if my salary is incorrect? Report any payroll discrepancy to payroll@nexora.in within ten (10) business days of the salary credit date. Include your employee ID, the specific discrepancy, and supporting calculation. The payroll team will investigate and, if an error is confirmed, correct it in the next payroll cycle or issue an off-cycle payment for significant amounts. Q37: How do I submit expense reimbursement claims? Log in to the Keka HR expense module, create a new claim, select the appropriate expense category, enter the amount, upload scanned receipts, and submit for manager approval. All claims must be submitted within fifteen (15) calendar days of the expense date. Claims submitted after thirty (30) days may not be processed. Q38: Does Nexora provide fuel or vehicle allowance? A vehicle allowance is not part of the standard compensation structure. However, employees who use their personal vehicles for official travel within their city may claim reimbursement at the standard fuel rate of INR 8 per km for two-wheelers and INR 14 per km for four-wheelers, subject to manager approval and distance substantiation. Q39: How does income tax deduction work on my salary? Nexora Technologies deducts Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) from your monthly salary based on your declared investment proofs and the applicable income tax slab. You are required to submit your investment declarations at the beginning of the financial year (April) and actual proofs by January 31st of that year. Failure to submit proofs by the deadline may result in higher TDS deductions in the final months of the year. You can download Form 16 from the Keka HR portal after the financial year closes. 12.8 Policies and Procedures Q40: Where can I find the full list of approved software? The approved software catalog is maintained by the IT team and is accessible through the IT section of the company intranet. The catalog is updated quarterly. If you need a software tool that is not on the list, submit a software request through the IT service desk portal with a business justification, and the IT Security and Procurement teams will evaluate the request. Q41: How do I request a change to my employment details, such as my bank account or address? All employment record updates — including bank account changes, address updates, emergency contact changes, and PAN/Aadhaar updates — must be made through the Keka HR self-service

portal. Changes to bank account details additionally require a cancelled cheque and a signed authorization form submitted to the payroll team for verification before the change takes effect. Q42: Can I refer a friend or former colleague for a job at Nexora? Yes. Nexora Technologies operates an Employee Referral Program (ERP) that rewards employees for successful referrals. When your referred candidate is hired and completes their probationary period, you receive a referral bonus as per the ERP schedule published on the intranet. Referrals for roles where you are on the hiring panel are not eligible for the referral bonus. Immediate family members of the referring employee are not eligible for the program. Q43: What is the policy on accepting gifts from vendors or clients? You may accept gifts from vendors, clients, or partners up to a value of INR 2,000 per instance. Gifts exceeding this value must be declined or, where declining would cause significant embarrassment, returned with an explanatory note. Any gift received above INR 500 must be declared to the HR and Legal teams within five (5) business days of receipt. Gifts of cash or cash equivalents (such as gift cards, vouchers, or cryptocurrency) must never be accepted, regardless of value. Q44: Are employees allowed to take up freelance or consulting work outside Nexora? Secondary employment or freelance consulting work in areas unrelated to Nexora's business is generally permissible, provided it does not interfere with your Nexora work hours, performance, or professional obligations. However, any outside engagement that is in the same domain as Nexora's business, involves Nexora clients or partners, or could create a conflict of interest requires prior written disclosure to and approval from HR and your department head. Q45: What happens if I break company property accidentally? Accidental damage to company property — including laptops, monitors, mobile phones, and office equipment — should be reported to your manager and the IT/Facilities team immediately. An assessment will be conducted to determine whether the damage resulted from negligence or from normal use. In cases of negligence, the employee may be required to bear part or all of the replacement cost. Deliberate damage to company property constitutes gross misconduct. 12.9 Growth and Performance Q46: How do I know when I am eligible for a promotion? Promotion eligibility is assessed during the annual review cycle. To be considered, you must have received an Exceeds Expectations rating or above in at least two consecutive annual review cycles, be operating at or beyond the scope of your current level, and have the endorsement of your manager and department head. Promotions are not based solely on tenure. You can review the career framework for your function on the intranet to understand the competency expectations at the next level. Q47: What is the process for requesting a role change or internal transfer? Internal mobility at Nexora is actively encouraged. Employees who have completed at least twelve (12) months in their current role and wish to explore a different function, team, or location may apply for internal openings through the Talent Acquisition portal. Your current manager will be

notified after you have progressed to the interview stage. Internal candidates receive priority consideration and are assessed against the same criteria as external applicants. Q48: How are performance ratings calibrated to ensure fairness? Performance ratings are calibrated through a cross-functional calibration session held at the end of each annual review cycle. In calibration, all managers present their team's ratings to peers and senior leadership. Calibration ensures that ratings are consistent across teams, that high ratings are supported by concrete evidence, and that systemic biases are identified and corrected. The HR Business Partners facilitate calibration sessions and maintain records of the outcomes. Q49: Can I request feedback from people outside my immediate team? Yes. The performance management system supports a 360-degree feedback module that allows you to request structured feedback from peers, cross-functional partners, and stakeholders with whom you work regularly. Your manager can also initiate 360 feedback as part of your annual review. We encourage employees to actively seek feedback throughout the year, not only during formal review cycles. Q50: Is there a mentoring program at Nexora? Yes. Nexora operates a voluntary mentoring program that matches employees across levels and functions based on stated development goals and career interests. Applications for the mentoring program open twice a year (April and October) through the L&D portal. Participants commit to a minimum of one monthly meeting with their mentor over a six-month engagement. Senior employees at the Senior Manager level and above are strongly encouraged to serve as mentors and will receive recognition for mentorship participation in their annual review.
